title: Enoch and the Book of Enoch
lead: Enoch, the seventh from Adam, "walked with God. Then he was gone, for God took him" (Genesis 5:24). That brief mystery made him the hero of 1 Enoch, a Jewish collection of visions that Jude quotes.

sections.b: Genesis 5:18–24 gives Enoch a short, strange entry in the list from Adam to Noah. Instead of "and he died," it says he "walked with God" and "was not, for God took him." He lived 365 years, the number of days in a solar year. Hebrews 11:5 counts him among the heroes of faith: "he was taken up so that he would not see death." Luke 3:37 lists him in Jesus's family tree.

1 Enoch is a collection of five Jewish works written between about 300 BC and the time of Jesus: the Book of the Watchers (chapters 1–36), the Parables or Similitudes (37–71), the Astronomical Book (72–82), the Dream Visions (83–90) and the Epistle of Enoch (91–108). Aramaic fragments of most of these were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls. The full book survives only in Ge'ez, the old language of Ethiopia, and it is part of the Bible of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Other Jews and Christians did not include it in their Bibles, though many early Christian writers knew and valued it.
